answer: The basalt debit happens at intake, grove totals the burned amount, and wharf anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 16 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. A farm hence pays the burn once for each alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Honest users pay that once, farms 18 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
